description:
🌍 Douala Earth Watchers: a team from Douala using NASA satellite data to track rainfall 🌧️, temperature 🌡️ and vegetation 🌱 around the city.
🚀 Project: an interactive dashboard to spot areas at risk of flooding and extreme heat.
👨‍🎓 Student passionate about tech and data. Beginners welcome! 🤝

summary:
Douala Earth Watchers is an environmental monitoring project focused on the city of Douala, Cameroon. It uses NASA Earth observation data to monitor key environmental indicators, including air and land surface temperature, precipitation, and vegetation conditions.

The project aims to transform satellite data into clear visual insights through an interactive dashboard, helping users understand environmental changes, identify trends, and assess potential risks such as flooding and extreme heat.

By combining NASA datasets, geospatial analysis, and classical statistical forecasting methods, Douala Earth Watchers seeks to support environmental awareness and data-driven decision-making at the local level.
details:
Douala Earth Watchers is a web-based climate and environmental monitoring dashboard designed to help communities explore climate patterns in Douala, Cameroon. The project uses NASA Earth observation and climate datasets, including NASA POWER, MERRA-2, GPM IMERG, and MODIS vegetation data.

The dashboard presents historical temperature, precipitation, and vegetation indicators through interactive charts, filters, time-based visualizations, and a map interface. Users can compare different climate products, explore monthly trends, examine MODIS NDVI/EVI vegetation observations, and export the displayed data. The project also includes a scientific validation page with a precomputed daily temperature backtest and an experimental machine-learning laboratory for evaluating uploaded monthly datasets.

The main benefit of the project is that it makes complex satellite and reanalysis data easier to understand and use. It can support environmental awareness, climate education, local research, urban planning discussions, and early exploration of climate-related risks. The expected impact is to provide students, researchers, communities, and decision-makers with a transparent and accessible way to investigate climate conditions around Douala.

The project was developed using React, TypeScript, TanStack, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Plotly.js, Recharts, FastAPI, Python, Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and netCDF4. OpenStreetMap is used as the map background. The application is organized as a public, reproducible codebase with documented data sources, validation information, and limitations.

Our project is creative because it combines multiple NASA datasets in a single bilingual and user-friendly interface focused on a specific African city. It separates temperature, precipitation, and vegetation products instead of mixing datasets with different meanings and resolutions. The team also considered scientific transparency, data provenance, spatial resolution, missing values, cloud contamination in vegetation observations, the difference between reanalysis products and ground measurements, and the risk of presenting exploratory results as official forecasts. These considerations help ensure that the dashboard is useful while remaining responsible and scientifically cautious.
